steps.title: Identify the noun’s case role
steps.body: In the supplied Муж говорит, the husband is the subject and the talking verb states its action. The subject noun is nominative. Recognizing the English sentence meaning is useful, but the role check asks whether the noun is a subject or direct object. Do not guess nominative merely because a case is unfamiliar.

steps.title: Separate the subject from its description
steps.body: In Поезд старый, the train is the subject noun and old is its predicate description. This present property clause has no overt Russian copula. The noun’s case role is nominative subject, not accusative direct object. A dictionary-looking noun or familiar translation alone does not identify its role in every construction.

steps.title: Apply the distinction to a different supplied noun
steps.body: Студент новый supplies a second independent property clause: the student is the subject noun, and new describes that subject. Its case role is nominative subject. Keep Муж говорит — The husband is talking and Поезд старый — The train is old as correct sentence meanings; the optional reference choices do not demonstrate this case role. These supplied examples are deliberately taught, not unseen evidence or unrestricted productive case use. Other constructions have nominative predicate nouns; not every nominative noun is a subject.

steps.title: Review noun behavior
steps.body:
An indeclinable noun keeps the same form for case or number. In these examples, ра́дио and такси́ are indeclinable. Recognize the behavior of the shown noun.

The nouns метро́, кино́, пальто́ and ко́фе are also indeclinable. Their forms stay unchanged for case or number. Learn the noun with this behavior; do not infer that every noun with a similar ending behaves the same way.

кафе́ and меню́ are two more indeclinable nouns. An unchanged word form does not mean that a sentence has no case relationships. These checks classify the shown noun; they do not test production of a sentence or a complete paradigm.

Contrast кни́га and окно́: these nouns are declinable, so they can change for case. Their nominative and genitive forms differ. Choose the behavior of the shown noun: unchanged for case or number, or able to change for case. No new form needs to be invented.

steps.title: Admitted possession, objects, and direction
steps.body: Proposed Unit 6 uses frozen records for possession, objects, and direction. Qualified review is pending.
steps.bookDirection: Open Lesson 6 in the copy you own. The app records do not replace that lesson.

steps.title: My: agreement with the noun
steps.body: In мой стол, стол is masculine singular. In моя собака, собака is feminine singular. Both phrases mean my plus a noun, but the Russian form of my changes to match the noun.

steps.title: Match gender, number and case
steps.body: Possessives such as мо́й and тво́й agree with the noun they describe in gender, number and case. Choose the form from the noun, not from the gender of its owner. Start with the nominative forms below, then compare the feminine accusative example.

steps.title: Our: a worked case change
steps.body: Наш means our; Ваш means your. In the worked phrase на́ша сестра́, both words are feminine singular nominative. To put this phrase in the direct-object accusative, change both words: на́ша сестра́ becomes на́шу сестру́. Keep the same noun and feminine singular agreement. на́шего бра́та changes the referent, and на́ши is plural.

steps.title: Masculine and feminine forms
steps.body: In the nominative singular, мо́й is masculine and моя́ is feminine. For стол choose мо́й; for собака choose моя́. The form follows the noun being described.

steps.title: Neuter and plural forms
steps.body: моё is the neuter singular nominative form of my. мои́ is the plural nominative form. A singular noun does not take the plural form in these choices.

steps.title: Your: masculine and feminine
steps.body: тво́й is masculine singular nominative; твоя́ is feminine singular nominative. Both mean your. To change the masculine form to the feminine form while keeping nominative singular, choose твоя́.

steps.title: Guided practice
steps.body: Choose the form that matches the noun. Then read why the other forms do not fit.

steps.title: Review the agreement rule
steps.body:
Possessives such as мо́й and тво́й agree with the noun they describe in gender, number and case. Choose the form from the noun, not from the gender of its owner. Start with the nominative forms below, then compare the feminine accusative example.

In мой стол, стол is masculine singular. In моя собака, собака is feminine singular. Both phrases mean my plus a noun, but the Russian form of my changes to match the noun.

In the nominative singular, мо́й is masculine and моя́ is feminine. For стол choose мо́й; for собака choose моя́. The form follows the noun being described.

моё is the neuter singular nominative form of my. мои́ is the plural nominative form. A singular noun does not take the plural form in these choices.

Наш means our; Ваш means your. In the worked phrase на́ша сестра́, both words are feminine singular nominative. To put this phrase in the direct-object accusative, change both words: на́ша сестра́ becomes на́шу сестру́. Keep the same noun and feminine singular agreement. на́шего бра́та changes the referent, and на́ши is plural.

тво́й is masculine singular nominative; твоя́ is feminine singular nominative. Both mean your. To change the masculine form to the feminine form while keeping nominative singular, choose твоя́.

sessions.title: Choose the admitted animate or inanimate object form

steps.title: Identify the inanimate table object
steps.body: сто́л is the supplied masculine inanimate table form. Its singular nominative and accusative have the same spelling and stress. A direct object can be accusative even when its form matches nominative. Dictionary English notes name a sense; they are not complete sentence translations.

steps.title: Contrast masculine singular animacy
steps.body: In these supplied singular masculine examples, an inanimate accusative matches nominative; an animate accusative matches genitive. Matching a genitive form does not change the accusative syntactic role. This is bounded recognition of supplied forms, not a rule that every animate noun in every gender or number takes an ending you can generate.

steps.title: Keep the inanimate house form
steps.body: до́м is the supplied masculine inanimate house form. Its singular accusative matches its singular nominative. This spelling identity does not by itself tell you a word’s sentence role; use the requested case or supplied context.

steps.title: Recognize the animate brother pair

In these supplied singular masculine examples, an inanimate accusative matches nominative; an animate accusative matches genitive. Matching a genitive form does not change the accusative syntactic role. This is bounded recognition of supplied forms, not a rule that every animate noun in every gender or number takes an ending you can generate.
